transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2026-03-04
Time: 15:00 UTC
Duration: ~45 minutes
Attendees: Lena Ortiz (Redwood AE), Mark Huang (Redwood SE), Diego Ramos (Redwood partner eng - joined briefly), Priya Narang (AstraCloud PM), Tom Sutter (AstraCloud LSE), Sarah Lee (AstraCloud Marketplace Ops)

Summary:
- Technical integration sync between Redwood and AstraCloud for marketplace listing, reference architecture, and joint solution packaging.
- Covered listing requirements (billing, SKUs, logos), required security/compliance docs, reference architecture for hosted vs private deployments, and next steps to run a pre-prod demo.
- Action items assigned for checklist, demo, and PR coordination.

Topics:
- Marketplace listing checklist and timeline
- Reference architecture (hosted API vs dedicated/private) and deployment options
- SSO/billing/KMS and audit log expectations
- Demo plan and test accounts

Action items (repeated in notes): see metadata above

Transcript:
[00:00] Lena Ortiz: okay everyone thanks for joining, um today is the integration sync for Redwood and Astra marketplace listing, we wanted to run through the checklist, the reference architecture, and the path to get a joint listing live.
[00:18] Priya Narang: great thanks Lena, we are excited — we have Sarah and Tom with us, we'll take notes on ops and engineering side.
[00:25] Tom Sutter: hey all, quick context: AstraCloud marketplace team wants to onboard Redwood as a managed inference partner. primary asks: clear billing, security artifacts, and a reference arch that maps to our private marketplace bundle.
[00:40] Mark Huang: perfect, will cover the technical mapping. quick intro — Redwood provides hosted API, Redwood Dedicated for reserved capacity, and Redwood Private which is VPC/on-prem oriented. for marketplace we usually recommend a reference architecture that shows both hosted and private deployment flows.
[00:55] Sarah Lee: can you clarify the difference from a partner listing standpoint? does Redwood host the model and we just resale? or do we need to host images in our marketplace?
[01:10] Lena Ortiz: good q. short answer: multiple options. 1) hosted API listing — Redwood remains the runtime and we bill usage via a marketplace SKU (metering integration required). 2) dedicated bundle — reserved capacity, customer is billed on commit via marketplace. 3) private/on-prem — customer deploys Redwood Private; marketplace listing points to an entitlement flow and support contract.
[01:35] Priya Narang: and for hosted API billing, what do you need from our side?
[01:42] Mark Huang: we need a billing SKU and partner account ID, plus a metering endpoint hookup — in practice we supply a small integration spec (we have a standard marketplace meters endpoint) and Astra provides the SKU and pricing. also need product images, logos, short description, and an approved terms doc.
[02:05] Tom Sutter: sounds good. can you share the spec after this call?
[02:09] Lena Ortiz: yes, we'll send listing_checklist.docx and a lightweight integration spec.
[02:13] Diego Ramos: i'll add the spec link to the doc pack, can share samples from prior listings.
[02:18] Sarah Lee: great. next, security — our reviewers will want SOC2, ISO, and details on encryption at rest, KMS, and audit logs. do you have those?
[02:30] Mark Huang: yes, Redwood has SOC2 Type II in our docs, we support CMKs via KMS/HSM integrations for Private deployments and audit logs through Redwood Console. note: some of the filenames in our docs have typos in older versions, so if you see somethin like K V cache spelled weird that's from the auto-gen.
[02:48] Priya Narang: any special network requirements for Private?
[02:52] Mark Huang: for Redwood Private we do a control plane handshake and then the runtime sits in the customer's VPC; we require outbound egress for telemetry if you opt-in, but a fully air-gapped install is possible with an occasional offline license exchange. we'll put those options in the ref_arch_diagram.png we'll share.
[03:12] Tom Sutter: okay good. what about SSO? our marketplace requires SAML/SSO for onboarding admin users.
[03:20] Lena Ortiz: Redwood supports SAML SSO and OIDC; for Dedicated and Private we integrate with your IdP. for hosted API, we offer SSO for the console and can map roles via RBAC.
[03:33] Sarah Lee: great. can you also confirm data residency controls? some customers require EU-only.
[03:40] Mark Huang: yes, we have region pinning and routing policies — you can pin requests to EU regions and we have region-specific deployment options for both hosted and dedicated. we'll note that in the listing.
[03:56] Priya Narang: next let's talk reference architecture. Tom, Mark — do you want to walk through options?
[04:05] Mark Huang: sure. i'll share screen after notes but high level: option A — Hosted Marketplace listing: Redwood runtime in our hosted cloud; Astra handles the UX and the marketplace routes calls to Redwood via the partner route; option B — Dedicated bundle: reserved GPU pools for Astra customers — provisioning and capacity contract flows; option C — Private/On-prem: Astra customers deploy a package behind their VPC and Redwood control plane manages licenses.
[04:32] Tom Sutter: for Dedicated bundle, what does provisioning look like from a customer lifecycle standpoint — is it automated or manual?
[04:40] Mark Huang: provisioning can be automated via infra-as-code we supply a terraform module and API hooks. there's a small ops step for quota assignment but it's largely automated. we'll provide the module in the repo and a terraform example.
[04:55] Sarah Lee: for marketplace listing, do you support subscription vs usage billing?
[05:00] Lena Ortiz: yes both. subscription for a reserved capacity SKU or monthly support; usage for per-token or per-embedding billing. marketplace often prefers SKU mapping for metered usage so that billing flows through their system.
[05:14] Priya Narang: okay let's cover compliance artifacts — will you share SOC2 and pen-test reports?
[05:20] Mark Huang: we can share SOC2 summary and a pen-test attestation under NDA; full reports go through legal. we'll put the security pack link in the doc pack.
[05:32] Tom Sutter: perfect. also need audit log format — our compliance team wants to see event schema.
[05:38] Mark Huang: audit logs are exportable from Redwood Console; they include request IDs, user IDs, timestamps, model variant, and tokens counts. i can paste a sample schema in the checklist. note: token counts sometimes show as "tokencount" in older exports - small naming variance.
[05:58] Priya Narang: demo plan — we want a pre-prod demo showing a customer journey: from marketplace purchase to provisioning a test tenant and running a simple inference workload.
[06:08] Lena Ortiz: we'll do that. Mark will run the demo of provisioning + SSO + a sample inference. we recommend using our small LLM demo model to validate latency and routing.
[06:20] Tom Sutter: do you have any performance artifacts or benchmark numbers to share? some customers ask about p99 latency for 1k token sequences.
[06:30] Mark Huang: yes, we have perf profiles for several model families. i'll attach a perf_sheet.csv to the follow-up — it includes p50/p95/p99 for typical sequence lengths and HW types, but note p99 is sensitive to batching and KV cache; also our kernel selection info is in the doc pack.
[06:52] Sarah Lee: regarding images and marketing assets — what formats and dimensions do you need?
[06:57] Lena Ortiz: typical requirements: 1200x628 hero image, 512x512 logo (png/svg), short description 1-2 lines, long blurb 200-400 words, and contact link. we'll include these in listing_checklist.docx.
[07:12] Priya Narang: any special legal T&Cs we should be aware of?
[07:16] Lena Ortiz: standard partner terms, IP and support SLA options; for Private deployments we have a separate license addendum. legal review is recommended early.
[07:25] Priya Narang: okay good. next — joint solution packaging. we want a one-pager reference arch + sample customer flow for Astra's marketplace.
[07:34] Mark Huang: we can produce a joint one-pager (joint_solution_onepager.pdf) that maps the flow: marketplace purchase -> entitlement -> provisioning -> onboarding -> monitoring in Redwood Console. include typical SLOs and example costs.
[07:48] Tom Sutter: on costs — do you have guidance for quantization and batching to reduce unit cost? some customers will want low-cost inference.
[07:58] Mark Huang: yes, Redwood Optimize provides recommendations: quantization profiles per model and batching/caching suggestions. we can include recommended configs (e.g., 4-bit quantized variant + continuous batching for throughput workloads). also mention tradeoffs: lower precision may affect quality for some prompts.
[08:18] Sarah Lee: for the listing page do you want to call out model families or say "Redwood-hosted models"?
[08:24] Lena Ortiz: recommend we list supported model families and note that we have Redwood-verified performance profiles. avoid listing too many model names if licensing is in question; we'll propose an approved list in the doc pack.
[08:37] Priya Narang: okay turning to timeline — Astra wants the listing live by end of March if possible. is that feasible?
[08:46] Lena Ortiz: feasible if we move quickly on checklist items and get test accounts by next week. main blockers: legal review, marketplace SKU mapping, and test tenant provisioning.
[08:56] Tom Sutter: we can prioritize legal and provide SKUs; engineering can provide tenant IDs.
[09:02] Mark Huang: we'll aim for a pre-prod demo week of 2026-03-16 and then production listing after validation.
[09:09] Priya Narang: sounds good. quick question from engineering — how do you handle model fallbacks if capacity is constrained?
[09:17] Mark Huang: Redwood supports smart routing and fallbacks: by policy we can route to a lower-cost or smaller model variant and include automatic fallback to a compatible variant. routing rules can be per-tenant. we'll show routing config in the ref arch. small note: sometimes transcriptions in our docs show 'k v cash' vs 'K V cache' — ignore that.
[09:36] Sarah Lee: audit and observability — will Astra be able to surface token-level cost per customer?
[09:42] Mark Huang: yes, Redwood Console shows token-level cost and latency breakdowns per token per route; you can export reports and we also have tracing hooks.
[09:52] Tom Sutter: great. next — test accounts and creds: how will we provision test API keys?
[09:59] Lena Ortiz: we create a partner test tenant and generate restricted API keys for the demo. Tom, send the tenant info and we'll seed keys.
[10:08] Tom Sutter: will do.
[10:10] Priya Narang: any blockers on the Redwood side for marketplace listing presets?
[10:15] Lena Ortiz: none major, we have a standard listing template. need your marketing blurb, logo, and SKU.
[10:22] Diego Ramos: sharing sample repo links now — i'll paste links into the follow-up email.
[10:30] Priya Narang: great. quick legal Q: pen-test attestation under NDA — what's typical turnaround?
[10:36] Mark Huang: typically 3-5 business days for an attestation once NDA is in place; full reports require legal review.
[10:45] Sarah Lee: ok noted.
[10:47] Priya Narang: anything else on integration?
[10:50] Mark Huang: one technical caveat — for high-throughput customers we recommend Dedicated with autoscaling policies; for lower-latency critical apps we recommend region pinning and smaller batch sizes. also mention quantization may change memory footprint, so we can provide sizing guidance.
[11:10] Tom Sutter: how does autoscaling play with marketplace billing? if a customer spikes, will marketplace bill top-up?
[11:18] Lena Ortiz: yes it depends on SKU type — usage SKU will bill for actual usage, reserved capacity has commit-based billing; marketplace will need to support overage or burst billing flows if that's expected. we'll document recommended SKU semantics.
[11:32] Priya Narang: good. final admin — who will be the POC on each side?
[11:38] Lena Ortiz: Redwood POC: Lena Ortiz and Mark Huang (tech).
[11:43] Priya Narang: Astra POC: Priya Narang (partner) and Tom Sutter (eng).
[11:48] Lena Ortiz: ok, recap and next steps — we'll send listing_checklist.docx, ref_arch_diagram.png, joint_solution_onepager.pdf, perf_sheet.csv, and security_pack.zip. we'll also schedule the pre-prod demo week of 2026-03-16.
[12:05] Tom Sutter: thanks everyone.
[12:07] Sarah Lee: thanks.
[12:10] Meeting end.
